title: WhatsApp users can now reserve usernames
byline: WhatsApp has announced the introduction of username reservations, allowing users to secure a unique username ahead of the global rollout of its new username feature later this year.

title: Bird nests of fibre-optic cables show war’s impact on Ukraine
byline: Woven from fibre-optic cable and grass, a small ​bird’s nest found near the front line of the war in Ukraine shows how the more ‌than four-year-old conflict is reshaping the natural environment, researchers say.

title: US deports first migrant to Pacific nation Palau
byline: The United States has started deporting migrants to a sparsely populated archipelago in the tropical Pacific, the island nation of Palau told AFP on Wednesday.

title: Dangerous heatwave to hit US ahead of holiday weekend
byline: A prolonged and dangerous heatwave will intensify across a swathe of the US this week, ushering in scorching daytime heat, high humidity and stifling overnight temperatures, forecasters predict.

title: Strong winds and rough seas forecast around Sri Lanka during next 24 hours
byline: The Meteorology Department has forecast strong winds and rough sea conditions in several sea areas around Sri Lanka during the next 24 hours.

title: Trump made more than $1bn from crypto in first year back in office
byline: US President Donald Trump made more than $1bn (£750m) last year from business dealings in cryptocurrency, according to his mandatory financial report for 2025.

title: Sri Lanka weathers Middle East shock better than expected: IMF
byline: Sri Lanka’s economic recovery has remained resilient despite the fallout from the Middle East conflict, with strong revenue collection and growth helping cushion the impact of external shocks, although significant reform challenges remain, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said yesterday.

title: Construction firms report strong project pipeline despite mounting cost pressures
byline: Sri Lanka’s construction sector regained momentum in May as a steady flow of new project awards helped drive activity back into expansion territory, offering fresh evidence that investment activity remains resilient despite higher borrowing costs and global uncertainty.

title: Food and energy costs push Sri Lanka inflation to 6.8% in June
byline: Headline inflation accelerated further in June, rising above the Central Bank’s 5 percent target as higher domestic energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict continued to feed through to the economy.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Golden Boot Race: Top Scorers, Standings and Records
byline: Some of football’s biggest names are still chasing the game’s most coveted individual scoring prize, and for football-mad audiences in Sri Lanka following the tournament through the night, the race has become just as gripping as the results table itself.

title: Dead dolphin found washed ashore in Wilpattu national park
byline: A dead dolphin was found washed ashore in the Kollankanatta area of Wilpattu National Park on Monday evening (30), wildlife officials said.

title: Roof collapse kills 14 children at Pakistan tuition centre
byline: Fourteen children died after the roof of a building near Lahore collapsed on top of them, officials say.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Round of 16 Bracket and Schedule: Road to the Final Takes Shape
byline: For the first time in the tournament’s history, 48 nations are chasing 32 knockout spots. Here is the complete bracket, schedule, and survival guide for Sri Lankan fans tracking the run to the Finals.

title: Bird nests of fibre-optic cables show war’s impact on Ukraine
byline: Woven from fibre-optic cable and grass, a small ​bird’s nest found near the front line of the war in Ukraine shows how the more ‌than four-year-old conflict is reshaping the natural environment, researchers say.

title: US deports first migrant to Pacific nation Palau
byline: The United States has started deporting migrants to a sparsely populated archipelago in the tropical Pacific, the island nation of Palau told AFP on Wednesday.

title: Trump made more than $1bn from crypto in first year back in office
byline: US President Donald Trump made more than $1bn (£750m) last year from business dealings in cryptocurrency, according to his mandatory financial report for 2025.

title: Sugeeshwara Bandara further remanded
byline: Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena  today further remanded Sugeeshwara Bandara, leader of the Nava Janatha Peramuna and former private secretary to former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa, till July 8 over allegations that he received salaries for two positions under the Presidential expenditure vote.

title: Sarana Gunawardena files appeal against 16 years jail sentence
byline: Former Deputy Minister Sarana Gunawardena, who was found guilty and sentenced to 16 years’ imprisonment in connection with four corruption cases, has filed four separate appeals before the Court of Appeal challenging the Colombo High Court judgment.

title: MLT annual transfers effective from August 1
byline: Medical Laboratory Technologist (MLT) officers in the Western Province whose transfer orders do not specify an effective date will be transferred from August 1, 2026, without having to wait for their successors to assume duties, according to a notification issued by the Western Provincial Health Department.

title: Dengue cases surpass 55,000 mark as June records highest monthly tally
byline: Sri Lanka’s dengue caseload has exceeded 55,000, with June alone accounting for more than 21,500 infections, according to the latest figures released by the National Dengue Surveillance System.

title: ADB approves US$200Mn for Sri Lanka’s Cyclone Ditwah recovery
byline: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a US$200 million emergency assistance package to help Sri Lanka rebuild infrastructure, restore livelihoods and support communities affected by Cyclone Ditwah.

title: Politicians and the media - A love- hate relationship
byline: It is with humour that I listened to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake deliver his almost monthly speech in Parliament last week stating that if the media does not come out of the garbage pile they are in, they would not survive.

title: UN subcommittee on prevention of torture concludes second visit to Sri Lanka
byline: The United Nations Subcommittee on Prevention of Torture (SPT) concluded its second official visit to Sri Lanka on June 24, 2026, following a 10-day mission aimed at assessing the country’s efforts to prevent torture and ill-treatment, Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Ministry Colombo said.

title: Qatar airways restores 35 weekly flights to Colombo
byline: Qatar Airways has resumed full operations on the Doha–Colombo route from July 1, reinstating its schedule of five daily flights and strengthening air connectivity to Sri Lanka.

title: Sri Lanka reaffirms commitment to sustainable environment at UNESCAP ministerial session
byline: Sri Lanka has reaffirmed its steadfast commitment to ensuring a sustainable environment and advancing climate resilience through regional cooperation, Deputy Minister of Environment Anton Jayakody said while addressing the 9th Session of the Committee on Environment and Development at the Ministerial Level organized by the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UNESCAP).

title: Fmr. Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody grilled by Presidential Commission on coal deals
byline: The Presidential Commission of Inquiry probing alleged irregularities in coal procurement questioned former Energy Minister Engineer Kumara Jayakody for nearly two hours and recorded his statement yesterday (30).

title: Iran says it won’t meet with U.S. envoys
byline: Iran said Tuesday it would not meet with top ‌US envoys who flew to the region following an outbreak of hostilities, clouding the prospects for a lasting peace between the two countries.

title: PHIs raid tobacco betel dansala; suspect taken to Court
byline: An individual who held a dansala in Saliyawewa area to serve quids of betel containing tobacco on Poson Full Moon Poya day ended up in courts.

title: Labour shortage compels Sri Lankan firms to recruit foreign workers - Minister
byline: Sri Lanka’s private sector currently has more than 400,000 job vacancies, compelling local industries to recruit foreign workers from countries such as India and China due to a shortage of both skilled and unskilled labour, Minister of Industries and Entrepreneurship Development Sunil Handunnetti said.

title: Agrarians reject Yala paddy prices, demand Rs. 140 per kg
byline: The National Agrarians’ Unity has rejected the government’s guaranteed paddy prices for the 2026 Yala cultivation season, describing them as unrealistic in the face of rising production costs, and has warned of trade union action if the pricing policy is not revised.

title: Argument in Dansala queue ends in assault: Five arrested
byline: Five suspects have been arrested after a young man was allegedly assaulted outside a Poson Dansala in Malabe, following an incident that was widely circulated on social media.

title: Court orders Suresh Sallay to hand over phone, computer passwords to CID
byline: Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena today ordered former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director Suresh Sallay, who is being detained and questioned under a detention order over the Easter Sunday terrorist attacks, to provide the Criminal Investigation Department with the passwords to his mobile phone and computer for the purposes of the investigation.

title: Actor Gamini Samarakoon passes away
byline: Popular stage, teledrama and film actor Gamini Samarakoon passed away today.

title: US and Iran enter technical talks to secure peace deal, restart shipping
byline: The U.S. and Iran held technical talks ​in Doha on Wednesday as they seek to agree on the flow of shipping through the Strait of ‌Hormuz and secure a lasting ceasefire, a source with direct knowledge of the talks and an Iranian official said.

title: Meteorology Department gets new DG
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the appointment of A.L.K. Wijemannage as the new Director General of the Meteorology Department with immediate effect.

title: Cabinet approves rabies eradication and dog registration bill
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the publication of the Rabies Eradication and Dog Registration Bill in the Government Gazette before it is presented to Parliament for approval.

title: Cabinet green lights to 2027 student shoe programme
byline: The Cabinet has approved the implementation of a programme to provide a pair of footwear each to selected school students, as well as to lay and monastic students of Pirivenas and Seelamathas for the year 2027.

title: Pakistan says it intercepted four drones fired from Afghanistan
byline: Afghanistan’s Taliban says they have launched air strikes on Pakistani territory, as Islamabad said its forces had intercepted four rudimentary drones in the southern province of Balochistan.

title: Cabinet approves bus fare revision following fuel price hike
byline: The Cabinet has approved a proposal submitted by the Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister to revise bus fares in line with recent fuel price changes that came into effect on June 30, 2026.

title: Language barriers still affect citizen access to services: Minister
byline: Public Administration, Local Government and Provincial Councils Minister Chandana Abayaratne said that when citizens are unable to access government services in a language they understand, they may feel marginalised within their own country.

title: Dehiwala Zoo to announce names of popular lion cubs on July 3
byline: The National Zoological Gardens Department will announce the selected names for the two lion cubs born recently at the Dehiwala National Zoological Park, which have attracted widespread public attention and affection. The names were selected from suggestions submitted by animal lovers, and prizes will be awarded to those whose entries were chosen.

title: Dehiwala Zoo invites schoolchildren to name newborn hippo calf
byline: The National Zoolical Gardens Department has announced a special opportunity for schoolchildren to name the Nile hippopotamus calf recently born at the Dehiwala National Zoological Park as part of the zoo’s 90th anniversary celebrations.

title: Over 60% chance of strong El Niño; Govt. launches national preparedness drive
byline: Sri Lanka faces a 63% probability of a strong El Niño and a 33% probability of a weak El Niño, according to the latest assessment.

title: Spain records more than 1,000 heat-related deaths in June
byline: More than 1,000 deaths in Spain were attributed to the recent heatwave that roasted Europe, as the country posted the hottest first six months ever recorded, officials said on July 1.

title: Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith attends Pope Leo XIV’s extraordinary consistory at Vatican
byline: Archbishop of Colombo, Cardinal Malcolm Ranjith, participated in the Second Extraordinary Consistory convened by His Holiness Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican on June 26 and 27.

title: Suresh Sallay ends hunger strike
byline: Former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director Suresh Sallay, who launched a hunger strike while in the custody of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) over the Easter Sunday terror attack investigations, has decided to end his fast on the advice of his legal counsel.

title: Delay in resuming Talaimannar train services
byline: Despite the completion of repair and maintenance work on the Talaimannar railway line, which was damaged by severe weather last year, train services have yet to resume, drawing criticism from railway trade unions.

title: Badulla Alugolla fire spreads over 20 acres
byline: A fire that broke out in the Alugolla forest reserve area of Badulla this afternoon (1) has so far destroyed nearly 20 acres of land, according to the Disaster Management Center (DMC).

title: Newly appointed Navy Commander calls on Defence Secretary
byline: Newly appointed Commander of the Navy, Vice Admiral Damian Fernando, paid a courtesy call on the Defence Secretary, Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha (Retd), at the Ministry of Defence today (01 July).

title: Australia one win away from history! INFOGRAPHIC
byline: Australia have booked their place in the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup final after extending their unbeaten run to six matches, moving within one victory of a record seventh title.

title: Vice Admiral Damian Fernando assumes office as new Navy Commander
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake promoted the Chief of Staff of the Sri Lanka Navy, Rear Admiral Damian Fernando to the 3 star rank of Vice Admiral and appointed him as the 27th Commander of the Sri Lanka Navy with effect from 01 Jul 26.

title: BIA set for Rs. 15bn terminal upgrade
byline: Sri Lanka’s aviation sector is set to undergo significant infrastructure development, with plans underway to modernize the first passenger terminal of Bandaranaike International Airport with an investment of approximately Rs. 15 billion over the next two years, Ports and Civil Aviation Deputy Minister Janitha Ruwan Kodituwakku said.

title: Two Kelani Valley train services suspended due to lack of power set
byline: The Railway Department has announced the cancellation of two train services operating on the Kelani Valley line from today until further notice due to the unavailability of a power set required for operations.

title: State of emergency to end this month
byline: The state of emergency imposed following the Cyclone Ditwah disaster will not be extended beyond this month, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said today.

title: Mexico, France Cruise into World Cup Last 16
byline: Mexico and France secured emphatic victories to book their places in the World Cup last 16, delivering commanding performances in the knockout stage.

title: SLAF executes heroic CASEVAC mission
byline: The SLAF Sri Aviation Unit deployed under MINUSCA successfully conducted a Casualty Evacuation (CASEVAC) mission in Am Dafok yesterday (30 June 2026).

title: CSE ends mixed after technical delay curtails trading session
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange concluded Thursday’s session on a mixed note after a delayed market opening shortened trading hours due to a technical issue in the CSE trading system.

title: Central Bank warns public over prohibited pyramid schemes
byline: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka has issued a public notice warning that several companies and digital platforms have been identified and determined to be operating prohibited pyramid schemes under Section 83(C) of the Banking Act No. 30 of 1988, as amended.

title: Three die in Mexico City World Cup celebrations
byline: A 19-year-old woman is among three people to have died from suffocation during World Cup celebrations in Mexico City on Tuesday.
